newsitem.title: USA: Intel says Q1 performance is "on track".
newsitem.headline: Intel says Q1 performance is "on track".

text.p: Intel Corp Director of Investor Relations Gordon Casey says the company is still "on track" with its business plan for the first quarter of 1997.

"We're on track," Casey told Reuters after making a presentation to investors at the Robertson Stephens technology conference here, adding that the semiconductor company has seen no change in its first-quarter plans since it reported full-year 1996 in mid-January.

Casey noted that even based on the conservative guidance the company gave in January, that revenues would be roughly flat sequentially from the fourth quarter, this represented a large year-on-year jump.

Intel posted revenues of $4.64 billion in the first quarter of 1996, and if first quarter 1997 revenues were roughly even with its $6.44 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996, this would be a jump of about 39 percent.

Casey also said the company's new Pentium MMX multimedia processor, formally introduced in early January, was receiving "excellent acceptance" in the marketplace. "PCs are selling through very rapidly," he said in the presentation to analysts.
He said that its Pentium II processor - a Pentium Pro family chip with MMX technology formerly known by the code-name Klamath, is expected to be rolled out in the second quarter of this year.
Intel will be providing a new type of packaging for the new 32-bit processor, which he said would be used for the P6 family into the future and which would provide certain performance advantages.
He said Intel will be advancing into .25 process technology in the second half of 1997.

Casey said the company will also address the market for less-costly-to administer Personal Computers with its NetPC initiative and would address the "Segment 0" market for computing devices under $1,000.
